subject: Reasoning
q: Philately : Stamps :: Numismatics : ?
explanation: Philately is the collection and study of stamps; numismatics is the study and collection of coins.

subject: Reasoning
q: Cartographer is to maps as lexicographer is to:
explanation: A cartographer compiles maps; a lexicographer compiles dictionaries.

subject: Reasoning
q: Gregarious : Sociable :: Taciturn : ?
explanation: Gregarious means sociable; taciturn means reserved and saying little (talkative is its opposite).

subject: Reasoning
q: Choose the pair related in the same way as Book : Library.
explanation: Books are kept and displayed in a library; paintings are kept and displayed in a gallery.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which pair has the same relationship as Wheat : Flour?
explanation: Flour is made by processing wheat; sugar is made by processing sugarcane.

subject: Reasoning
q: Select the pair that matches Cub : Lion.
explanation: A cub is a young lion and a foal is a young horse; Cat : Kitten has the order reversed.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which pair of words is related in the same way as Generous : Miserly?
explanation: Generous and miserly are opposites, as are humble and arrogant; the other pairs are synonyms.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which of the following is a necessary part of a “library”?
explanation: A library is by definition a collection of books (or other reading material); computers, chairs and fees are not essential.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which one is essential to an “election”?
explanation: An election cannot take place without voters; posters, rallies and television coverage are optional.

subject: Reasoning
q: A “shoe” must always have:
explanation: Every shoe has a sole; many shoes have no laces or buckle and are not made of leather.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which of these is a necessary part of a “book”?
explanation: A book must have pages; pictures, an index and a glossary are found only in some books.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which of the following is indispensable to a “race”?
explanation: A race needs competitors; spectators, medals and a stadium are not required.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which one of the following is a necessary feature of a “desert”?
explanation: A desert is defined by very low rainfall; many deserts are rocky or icy and have no sand, camels or oases.

subject: Reasoning
q: Choose the necessary part of a “newspaper”.
explanation: A newspaper must carry news; advertisements, photographs and cartoons are common but not essential.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which of these is always necessary for “fire”?
explanation: Burning needs oxygen; wood and petrol are only particular fuels and a matchstick only one way of lighting it.

subject: Reasoning
q: A “contract” cannot exist without:
explanation: A contract is an agreement between parties; lawyers, stamp paper and witnesses are not always needed.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which one is a necessary part of a “pendulum”?
explanation: A pendulum is a weight hung so that it swings freely; it need not be part of a clock and needs no spring or battery.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which of the following must a “guitar” have?
explanation: A guitar is played by its strings; an amplifier, case and pick are accessories.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which is a necessary condition for “rain”?
explanation: Rain falls from clouds; thunder, lightning and wind often accompany it but are not needed.

subject: Reasoning
q: An “island” always has:
explanation: An island is land surrounded by water; trees, beaches and mountains are not essential.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which of these is a necessary part of an “examination”?
explanation: An examination tests candidates by setting questions or tasks; oral and online tests need no hall, answer sheet or invigilator.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which part is essential to a “tree”?
explanation: Every tree has roots; not every tree bears flowers or fruit, and birds are not part of it.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which of the following is necessary to make “cheese”?
explanation: Cheese is made from milk; bread, knives and refrigerators are not needed to make it.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which of the following is not a part of a “tree”?
explanation: Trunk, bark and branches are parts of a tree; a fin is part of a fish.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which of these is not part of a “ship”?
explanation: Hull, deck and anchor are parts of a ship; a saddle is used on a horse or bicycle.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which of the following does not belong to the “eye”?
explanation: The retina, pupil and cornea are parts of the eye; the eardrum is part of the ear.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which one is not a part of a “flower”?
explanation: Petals, sepals and stamens are parts of a flower; bark covers a tree’s trunk and branches.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which of these does not belong to a “formal letter”?
explanation: A formal letter has a salutation, subject line and signature; a chorus is part of a song.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which of the following is not a part of a “bicycle”?
explanation: Pedals, chain and handlebar are bicycle parts; a rudder steers a boat or aircraft.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which one does not belong inside a plant “cell”?
explanation: The nucleus, cytoplasm and chloroplasts are found inside a plant cell; a neuron is itself a whole nerve cell of animals.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which of these is not a part of the human “heart”?
explanation: Atria, ventricles and valves are parts of the heart; alveoli are air sacs in the lungs.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which one does not belong to a “parliament”?
explanation: A parliament has a Speaker, members and a chamber; an umpire officiates in games.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which of the following is not a part of a “newspaper”?
explanation: Headlines, the editorial and the masthead are parts of a newspaper; a stanza is a unit of a poem.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which one does not belong to a “river”?
explanation: A river has a source, tributaries and a mouth; a summit is the top of a mountain.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which of these is not a part of a “computer”?
explanation: Processor, memory and motherboard are computer parts; a carburettor is part of a petrol engine.

subject: Reasoning
q: Select the pair whose relationship is different from the others.
explanation: Pen, knife and needle are paired with what they are used for; a library is where books are kept.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which pair does not follow the pattern of the rest?
explanation: The others pair an animal with its young; a den is a lion’s home.

subject: Reasoning
q: Find the odd pair: Hot : Cold, Tall : Short, Fast : Slow, Big : Large.
explanation: The other pairs are opposites; big and large mean the same.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which country–city pair is different from the others?
explanation: The others pair a country with its capital; the capital of Turkey is Ankara, not Istanbul.

subject: Reasoning
q: Choose the pair that has a different relationship.
explanation: The others pair a worker with the place of work; a passenger is a person, not a workplace.

subject: Reasoning
q: Pick the pair unlike the other three: Petal : Flower, Page : Book, Wheel : Car, Milk : Cow.
explanation: The others pair a part with the whole it belongs to; milk is a product of a cow, not a part of it.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which pair differs from the rest?
explanation: The others pair a unit with the quantity it measures; petrol is a substance, not a quantity.

subject: Reasoning
q: Select the pair that does not share the relationship of the others.
explanation: The others pair a creator with what he creates; a stage is where a singer performs.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which of these pairs is the exception: Barometer : Pressure, Ammeter : Current, Odometer : Distance, Stethoscope : Doctor?
explanation: The others pair an instrument with what it measures; the stethoscope is paired with its user.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: The library will remain closed on Friday for its annual stock-taking. Which conclusion follows from the statement?
o: The library will close permanently after Friday.
Books cannot be borrowed from the library on Friday.
The library has lost many books.
explanation: A closed library cannot lend books that day; the statement says the stock-taking is annual and says nothing about losses or permanent closure.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: People born between 1981 and 1996 are called millennials. Sana was born in 1990. Which conclusion follows logically?
o: People born in 1998 are also millennials.
Sana is older than every other millennial.
explanation: 1990 lies within 1981–1996, so by the stated definition Sana is a millennial; nothing is said about her parents, and 1998 falls outside the range.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: Only candidates who score at least 40 per cent in every paper are declared successful. Hamid scored 38 per cent in English. Which conclusion follows from the statement?
o: All the other candidates were successful.
Hamid has not been declared successful.
Hamid will pass if he retakes English.
Hamid scored less than 40 per cent in every paper.
explanation: “Only” makes 40 per cent in every paper a necessary condition; Hamid missed it in English, so he cannot be successful. The rest is not stated.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: No shop in this market opens before 10 a.m. The bakery is a shop in this market. Which conclusion follows from the statement?
o: The bakery is the busiest shop in the market.
The bakery does not open before 10 a.m.
The bakery opens exactly at 10 a.m.
explanation: What is true of every shop in the market is true of the bakery; the exact opening time is not given.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: A factory produces 500 bicycles a day and works six days a week. Which conclusion follows from the statement?
o: The factory produces 3,000 bicycles in a working week.
The factory is closed on Sundays.
The factory produces 3,500 bicycles a week.
The demand for bicycles is rising.
explanation: 500 × 6 = 3,000; the statement does not say which day is the holiday or anything about demand.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: Since the new flyover opened, the average travel time between the two ends of the road has fallen from 40 minutes to 25 minutes. Which conclusion follows from the statement?
o: Every driver now saves exactly 15 minutes.
On average, the journey along that road now takes less time than before.
The flyover was very costly to build.
Accidents on the road have stopped.
explanation: The fall in the average supports only a general reduction; an average does not mean every driver saves the same time, and cost and accidents are not mentioned.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: Some of the trees in the park are more than a hundred years old. Which conclusion follows from the statement?
o: Most of the trees in the park are old.
No tree in the park was planted recently.
All the trees in the park are over a hundred years old.
At least one tree in the park is over a hundred years old.
explanation: “Some” guarantees at least one; it does not tell us about most or all of the trees.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: The meeting can begin only when at least half of the members are present. Today the meeting began at 11 a.m. Which conclusion follows from the statement?
o: The meeting usually begins at 11 a.m.
At least half of the members were present at 11 a.m.
explanation: Since the meeting began, the necessary condition (at least half present) must have been met; nothing more follows.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: A survey of 1,000 households in a city found that 620 of them own a motorcycle. Which conclusion follows from the statement?
o: More than half of the surveyed households own a motorcycle.
Most households in the country own a motorcycle.
Exactly 620 people in the city own motorcycles.
explanation: 620 out of 1,000 is more than half of the households surveyed; the survey counts households, not people, and covers only that city.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: Unless it rains, the match will be played today. The match was not played today. Which conclusion follows from the statement?
o: The match was cancelled for lack of players.
The match will be played tomorrow.
explanation: “Unless it rains, the match is played” means that if it does not rain the match is played; since the match was not played, it must have rained.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: Every employee who has served the company for at least ten years receives a gold medal. Farah has served the company for twelve years. Which conclusion follows from the statement?
o: Only Farah receives a gold medal.
explanation: Twelve years is at least ten, so the rule applies to Farah; nothing is said about others or her retirement.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: The museum charges no entry fee to children under twelve. Omar, who is nine, visited the museum yesterday. Which conclusion follows from the statement?
o: Adults pay a very high fee.
Omar did not have to pay an entry fee.
Most visitors to the museum are children.
Omar went to the museum with his parents.
explanation: Nine is under twelve, so the free-entry rule covers Omar; the other statements are not given.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: A study found that students who slept at least seven hours before an examination scored higher, on average, than those who slept less. Which conclusion follows from the statement?
o: Every student who slept less failed.
Sleeping longer guarantees a higher score.
In that study, adequate sleep went together with better average scores.
The examination was easy for everyone.
explanation: The finding is about averages in one study; it does not guarantee any individual result or say anyone failed.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: All flights to Skardu were cancelled today because of poor visibility. Which conclusion follows from the statement?
o: Flights to Skardu will also be cancelled tomorrow.
Visibility at Skardu is always poor.
Road travel to Skardu was also stopped.
No scheduled flight left for Skardu today.
explanation: If all flights were cancelled, none flew today; the statement says nothing about other days or about roads.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: Under a new rule, a driver caught without a seat belt is fined Rs 2,000 for the first offence and Rs 5,000 for each later offence. Zahid has been fined twice under this rule. Which conclusion follows from the statement?
o: Zahid has been fined Rs 10,000 in all.
Zahid has been fined Rs 4,000 in all.
Zahid will lose his driving licence.
Zahid has been fined Rs 7,000 in all under this rule.
explanation: His first fine was Rs 2,000 and his second Rs 5,000, a total of Rs 7,000; licences are not mentioned.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: The school will either extend the break or shorten the syllabus, but not both. It has decided to shorten the syllabus. Which conclusion follows from the statement?
o: The break will not be extended.
The syllabus was too long for students.
explanation: “Either … or …, but not both” means choosing one rules out the other.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: Every student of Class X passed the mathematics test. Some students of Class X play cricket. Which conclusion follows from the statement?
o: Only cricket players passed the test.
No cricket player failed any test.
Some cricket players passed the mathematics test.
All cricket players passed the mathematics test.
explanation: The cricket players in Class X are students of Class X, and all of them passed; nothing follows about cricket players outside the class.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: The shop sells only fruit and vegetables. Sadia bought something from the shop. Which conclusion follows from the statement?
o: Sadia bought both fruit and vegetables.
Sadia goes to the shop every day.
explanation: The shop sells nothing else, so whatever she bought was fruit or vegetables; it need not have been both.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: Several cases of dengue fever have been reported in a residential area after the monsoon rains. Which course of action should be followed?
o: All residents should be made to leave the area permanently.
Local authorities should spray against mosquitoes and remove stagnant water in the area.
Nothing should be done because the monsoon will end.
Hospitals in the area should be closed to stop the infection.
explanation: Dengue is spread by mosquitoes that breed in stagnant water; spraying and clearing water tackles the cause without extreme measures.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: Many students in a school are failing mathematics because they cannot follow the lessons. Which course of action should be followed?
o: The failing students should be expelled.
The school should arrange extra (remedial) classes for these students.
Mathematics should be removed from the syllabus.
The pass mark should be abolished.
explanation: Extra teaching addresses the stated cause; the other options avoid or punish the problem instead of solving it.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: A bridge on a busy highway has developed serious cracks. Which course of action should be followed?
o: The highway should be closed permanently.
The cracks should simply be painted over.
No action is needed until the bridge actually fails.
Heavy traffic should be stopped on the bridge until it is inspected and repaired.
explanation: Stopping heavy loads and repairing the bridge protects lives while restoring the route; the others are either extreme or ignore the danger.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: Citizens complain that they have to wait for hours at an office to obtain their identity cards. Which course of action should be followed?
o: The office should be shut down.
More counters should be opened and an appointment system introduced.
Citizens who complain should be fined.
explanation: More counters and appointments reduce waiting time directly; the others are unreasonable or make matters worse.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: Farmers in a district lose a large part of their harvest every year because they have no proper storage facilities. Which course of action should be followed?
o: The import of food should be banned.
Farmers should be asked to sell their land.
Farmers should be told to grow less.
Storage facilities such as warehouses should be built in the district.
explanation: The loss is caused by lack of storage, so building storage is the practical remedy.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: Road accidents at a busy crossing have risen sharply since its traffic signals stopped working. Which course of action should be followed?
o: Drivers should be told to avoid the city.
Speed limits in the whole province should be halved.
The traffic signals should be repaired without delay.
The crossing should be closed to all traffic for good.
explanation: The rise followed the signal failure, so repairing the signals directly removes the cause.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: Several houses in a hill town were damaged by landslides after heavy rain. Which course of action should be followed?
o: Residents should rebuild at the same spots at once.
All construction in the country should be banned.
Families living on unstable slopes should be moved to safer places and the slopes surveyed.
The town’s schools should be closed for a year.
explanation: Relocating those at risk and surveying the slopes addresses the danger; rebuilding immediately at the same spots repeats the risk.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: A government hospital reports a shortage of blood in its blood bank. Which course of action should be followed?
o: All operations should be stopped permanently.
The blood bank should be closed.
The hospital should organise blood donation camps.
Patients should bring blood from abroad.
explanation: Donation camps increase the supply of blood, which is exactly what is short.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: It has been found that several shops in a market sell expired medicines. Which course of action should be followed?
o: Drug inspectors should check the shops and take legal action against the offenders.
The authorities should wait for more complaints before acting.
All medical stores in the country should be closed.
People should stop buying medicines altogether.
explanation: Inspection and legal action target the offenders; the others are extreme or leave a health risk unchecked.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: The water supply to a city is expected to fall short this summer because the reservoir level is low. Which course of action should be followed?
o: Water should be supplied only to factories.
The remaining water should be released at once.
Citizens should be urged to save water and supply schedules should be announced.
The shortage should be kept secret to avoid panic.
explanation: Conservation and planned supply stretch the limited water fairly; the others waste it or leave people unprepared.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: Research shows that children who read regularly at home do better at school. Which course of action should be followed?
o: Parents should be encouraged to build a reading habit at home.
Public libraries should be closed during school hours.
Children who do not read should be kept out of school.
explanation: Encouraging home reading acts on the finding; the other options do not follow from it.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: Many young graduates in a region remain unemployed because they lack the technical skills that local industries need. Which course of action should be followed?
o: Industries should be moved out of the region.
Graduates should be barred from applying for jobs.
Technical and vocational training should be expanded in the region.
Universities in the region should be closed.
explanation: Training supplies the missing skills, which is the stated cause of unemployment.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: Smoke from brick kilns is a major cause of winter smog around a city. Which course of action should be followed?
o: Citizens should stay indoors for the whole winter.
Kilns should be required to adopt cleaner firing methods and be inspected regularly.
All vehicles in the city should be banned permanently.
Brick production should be doubled to meet demand.
explanation: Cleaner firing and inspection reduce the stated source of smog; the others ignore the kilns or are extreme.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: An audit reveals that some officials of a department misused public funds. Which course of action should be followed?
o: An inquiry should be held and those found responsible should be punished.
The audit report should be kept secret.
All employees of the department should be dismissed.
explanation: An inquiry followed by punishment holds the guilty to account without harming the innocent or hiding the matter.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: “Please use the stairs; the lift is under repair.” Which assumption is implicit in the statement?
o: The lift will never be repaired.
The building has only one floor.
The stairs are available for use.
explanation: Advising people to use the stairs takes for granted that the stairs can be used.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: An advertisement says: “Buy our water filter to keep your family healthy.” Which assumption is implicit in the statement?
o: Other filters do not work at all.
Every home already owns a filter.
People want to keep their families healthy.
explanation: The advertisement appeals to the wish for a healthy family; it does not assume the extreme claims.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: The school announced that classes will be held online during the smog emergency. Which assumption is implicit in the statement?
o: Online teaching is better than classroom teaching in every way.
The smog will last all year.
Teachers do not want to come to school.
Students are able to attend classes online.
explanation: Moving classes online is sensible only if students can join them; the other ideas are not needed for the decision.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: The government has raised the tax on cigarettes in order to reduce smoking. Which assumption is implicit in the statement?
o: The government needs no other revenue.
A higher price will discourage some people from smoking.
explanation: The policy works only if price affects smoking; it need not assume that everyone quits.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: “If you want to learn swimming, join the evening classes at the club.” Which assumption is implicit in the statement?
o: Swimming can be learnt in the evening classes at the club.
explanation: The advice assumes the classes can teach swimming; it does not claim the club is the only place.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: The railway has introduced online booking so that passengers need not queue at stations. Which assumption is implicit in the statement?
o: Queues at bus stations will disappear too.
Many passengers are able to book tickets online.
explanation: The scheme reduces queues only if a good number of passengers can use it.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: A label reads: “Keep medicines out of the reach of children.” Which assumption is implicit in the statement?
o: Children could be harmed by taking medicines unsupervised.
explanation: The warning exists because children might swallow medicines and be harmed.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: The municipality has planted thousands of trees along main roads to reduce air pollution. Which assumption is implicit in the statement?
o: There were no trees in the city before.
Trees help to improve air quality.
Air pollution will end within a month.
explanation: Planting trees for this purpose assumes they help clean the air, not that pollution will vanish.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: A company has decided to open a branch in Gwadar to serve its growing number of customers there. Which assumption is implicit in the statement?
o: Customers in other cities are unhappy.
The new branch will attract enough customers to be worthwhile.
The company’s other branches will be closed.
There are no other companies in Gwadar.
explanation: Opening a branch presumes it will have enough business; the other points are not implied.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: An examination instruction says: “Write your roll number on every page of the answer book.” Which assumption is implicit in the statement?
o: Examiners do not read the answers.
The answer book has only one page.
Writing the roll number helps identify each page with the right candidate.
explanation: The instruction is useful only if roll numbers help match pages to candidates.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: “Book your tickets early to avoid disappointment.” Which assumption is implicit in the statement?
o: Tickets may sell out if one delays booking.
explanation: The advice assumes that late bookers may find no tickets left.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: The minister said that the new dam will help overcome the power shortage. Which assumption is implicit in the statement?
o: The dam will be completed next month.
There is no other way to produce electricity.
The dam will be used to generate electricity.
explanation: A dam can ease a power shortage only if it produces electricity; nothing is assumed about timing or other sources.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: The college has started a counselling service for students who feel stressed during examinations. Which assumption is implicit in the statement?
o: Teachers do not care about students.
Some students experience stress during examinations.
All students fail because of stress.
explanation: The service assumes there are stressed students who need it, not that all of them fail.

subject: Reasoning
q: Statement: “Shift the patient to the city hospital; the local clinic cannot handle such cases.” Which assumption is implicit in the statement?
o: The city hospital charges no fees.
The local clinic will be closed.
The patient is not seriously ill.
The city hospital can treat such cases.
explanation: Advising the transfer assumes the city hospital has the facilities that the clinic lacks.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which word cannot be made from the letters of CONSTITUTION, using each letter only as often as it appears?
explanation: NATION needs A more often than CONSTITUTION provides; UNIT, TONIC, NOTION can all be made from its letters.

subject: Reasoning
q: Using the letters of EDUCATION (each only as many times as it occurs), which of these words cannot be formed?
explanation: CONTINUE needs N more often than EDUCATION provides; CAUTION, AUCTION, NOTICE can all be made from its letters.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which word cannot be formed from the letters of INTERNATIONAL?
explanation: LATERAL needs L more often than INTERNATIONAL provides; ORIENTAL, NATIONAL, RELATION can all be made from its letters.

subject: Reasoning
q: From the letters of PARLIAMENT, which of the following words cannot be spelt?
explanation: PARTNER needs R more often than PARLIAMENT provides; LAMENT, PLANET, MARINE can all be made from its letters.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which one of these words cannot be made out of CHAIRMAN?
explanation: MACHINE needs E more often than CHAIRMAN provides; CHAIN, MARCH, CHARM can all be made from its letters.

subject: Reasoning
q: Taking letters only from DEMOCRACY, which word is impossible to form?
explanation: ACADEMY needs A more often than DEMOCRACY provides; CREAM, COMEDY, DECOY can all be made from its letters.

subject: Reasoning
q: Each letter of ENVIRONMENT may be used only as often as it appears. Which word cannot be formed?
explanation: RETENTION needs T more often than ENVIRONMENT provides; INVENT, MENTION, VERMIN can all be made from its letters.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which word is not formed from the letters of GEOGRAPHY?
explanation: PHOTO needs T, O more often than GEOGRAPHY provides; GRAPH, HOPE, PAGE can all be made from its letters.

subject: Reasoning
q: Out of the letters of KNOWLEDGE, which word cannot be made?
explanation: KNOWN needs N more often than KNOWLEDGE provides; LEDGE, WEDGE, KNEEL can all be made from its letters.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which of the following words CAN be formed from the letters of TEMPERATURE?
explanation: Only RAPTURE uses letters available in TEMPERATURE; PAMPER needs an extra P; MATURITY needs an extra I, Y; PERMIT needs an extra I.
